reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.145.1-3 re-derived. Ps 145 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json psalms.145 rule=identity, web_verses 21 / mt_verses 21, web_title true, mt_title_verses []), so web:Ps.145.0 = oshb:Ps.145.1 is the owner-ruled title form and no dual-cite arithmetic is at issue. Every Hebrew run in the row collates at byte tier against its cited ref: תְּהִלָּ֗ה לְדָ֫וִ֥ד (oshb:Ps.145.1, byte), אֲרוֹמִמְךָ֣ (oshb:Ps.145.1, byte), גָּ֘ד֤וֹל (oshb:Ps.145.3, byte; skeleton-only elsewhere at oshb:Ps.145.6, so the cited ref is the byte-grade one). The alef/bet/gimel run is confirmed from psalm_device_inventory.json acrostics.145.first_letters_mt, whose 21-letter string opens alef-bet-gimel and records letters_missing = nun; the row's per-row letter shares (3+4+6+3+5) tile that 21 exactly across the five Ps 145 rows. The tehillah exclusivity object is right: genre_label_membership.tehillah = [145], and superscriptions.145 carries labels [tehillah, le_david]. The seam at web:Ps.145.3|web:Ps.145.4 is real - דּ֣וֹר לְ֭דוֹר (oshb:Ps.145.4) introduces a new grammatical subject. Two defects: the sweep denominator for WEB titles is wrong, and the rejected_alternative mischaracterizes the verse on the left of its own seam.

challenges.claim: The rationale's sweep citation 'sweep: 1 of 150 WEB titles, genre-label inventory' states a false book-level count: the staged inventory carries 116 WEB titles, not 150.
challenges.evidence: psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions is a dict of length 116 (re-derived: len(inv['superscriptions']) == 116); superscriptions.146 is null, confirming untitled psalms are absent from the inventory rather than counted. The book strategy states the same figure - '116 WEB titles (Ps 119 has NONE ...)'. 150 is the psalm count, not the title count. The exclusivity conclusion survives (genre_label_membership.tehillah = [145], sweep: 1 psalm of the 116 titled), but the stated universe is overstated by 34 titles and the same wrong denominator is repeated in observed_substrate_signals[1] ('sweep: 1 of 150 titles').

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative's contrast at the web:Ps.145.3|web:Ps.145.4 seam mis-states the left edge: it says web:Ps.145.4 'turns from the psalmist's own first-person vow', but the row's own last verse web:Ps.145.3 is already third-person predication with no first-person form in its bytes.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.145.3 reads גָּ֘ד֤וֹל יְהוָ֣ה וּמְהֻלָּ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד וְ֝לִגְדֻלָּת֗וֹ אֵ֣ין חֵֽקֶר - no 1cs verb and no 1cs suffix anywhere in the verse; WEB agrees, “Great is Yahweh, and greatly to be praised! His greatness is unsearchable.” (web:Ps.145.3), against the first-person forms that do stand at oshb:Ps.145.1 (אֲרוֹמִמְךָ֣) and oshb:Ps.145.2 (אֲבָרֲכֶ֑ךָּ). The operative discriminator the row also names - a fresh grammatical subject at דּ֣וֹר לְ֭דוֹר (oshb:Ps.145.4), “One generation will commend your works to another, and will declare your mighty acts.” (web:Ps.145.4) - is sound; only the first-person framing of the left edge is byte-false, so the seam itself stands.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.145.4-7 re-derived. All four Hebrew runs collate byte-tier at their cited refs: דּ֣וֹר לְ֭דוֹר (oshb:Ps.145.4), הֲ֭דַר (oshb:Ps.145.5; accent_stripped-only elsewhere at oshb:Ps.145.12, so the cited ref is byte-grade), וּגְדוּלָּתְךָ֥ (oshb:Ps.145.6), זֵ֣כֶר (oshb:Ps.145.7). The dalet/he/waw/zayin sequence matches psalm_device_inventory.json acrostics.145.first_letters_mt positions 4-7. The ketiv/qere claim is inventory-valid: pmarks_Ps.json kq carries Ps.145.6 with 1 note (68 notes over 65 verses book-wide), and the verse is one of the inline-ketiv cases - the unpointed token stands in the verse bytes immediately before the pointed qere, exactly as the row describes, so the row's disclosure is correct and its inline-K/Q description matches the substrate. The rejected_alternative's left edge is accurate: oshb:Ps.145.7 carries third-person plural verbs (יַבִּ֑יעוּ, יְרַנֵּֽנוּ) against the nominal predication that opens oshb:Ps.145.8. One defect: the acrostic letter-bearing word for the waw line is misattributed.

challenges.claim: The rationale attaches 'opening the waw line' to the ketiv/qere pair at oshb:Ps.145.6, but neither of those tokens opens the verse; the waw the acrostic counts is carried by the verse-initial word.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.145.6 reads וֶעֱז֣וּז נוֹרְאֹתֶ֣יךָ יֹאמֵ֑רוּ וגדולתיך וּגְדוּלָּתְךָ֥ אֲסַפְּרֶֽנָּה. The verse-initial word is וֶעֱז֣וּז; the ketiv וגדולתיך and the qere וּגְדוּלָּתְךָ֥ stand fourth and fifth in the verse. The row quotes the acrostic-bearing word for every other letter in the span (דּ֣וֹר for dalet, הֲ֭דַר for he, זֵ֣כֶר for zayin) but substitutes the mid-verse K/Q pair for waw, so a reader re-deriving acrostics.145.first_letters_mt from the row's own quotes cannot recover the waw. The sequence claim itself is correct; only the word attribution is wrong.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.145.8-13 re-derived. Hebrew runs all byte-tier at their cited refs: חַנּ֣וּן (oshb:Ps.145.8), טוֹב (oshb:Ps.145.9), יוֹד֣וּךָ (oshb:Ps.145.10), מַֽלְכוּתְךָ֗ מַלְכ֥וּת כָּל עֹֽלָמִ֑ים (oshb:Ps.145.13). The het-through-mem run matches acrostics.145.first_letters_mt positions 8-13. The core held-zone handling is correct and I confirm it independently: the MT bytes at oshb:Ps.145.13 stop at וָדֽוֹר with no nun-initial material, and a skeleton sweep for the nun line's expected opening word returns 1 verse book-wide - MT Ps.89.38 (= web:Ps.89.37) - and 0 verses anywhere in Ps 145 (sweep: 1 verse, sweep.py --skel), while acrostics.145.letters_missing is nun. The row chunks the verse as WEB gives it and selects no reading, which is the required treatment. I also note, without filing it, that an undisclosed third-person-to-second-person pivot sits inside the span at web:Ps.145.9|web:Ps.145.10 (oshb:Ps.145.9 predicates about Yahweh, טוֹב יְהוָ֥ה לַכֹּ֑ל; oshb:Ps.145.10 addresses him directly, יוֹד֣וּךָ and מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ), so the row's only cohesion warrant across six verses is the acrostic run. The filed defect is in how the variant is described. Confidence medium is well calibrated here.

challenges.claim: The disclosure of the held nun-line zone is described against the bytes: observed_substrate_signals[1] says 'MT's own bytes at oshb:Ps.145.13 carry one sentence' and calls the extra WEB material 'the second, nun-initial sentence', but oshb:Ps.145.13 is a full bicolon that WEB renders as two sentences, and the variant material is WEB's third sentence.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.145.13 reads מַֽלְכוּתְךָ֗ מַלְכ֥וּת כָּל עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וּ֝מֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֗ בְּכָל דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר, divided by etnachta (U+0591, byte-verified on עֹֽלָמִ֑ים) into two cola; WEB renders exactly those two cola as two sentences, “Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. Your dominion endures throughout all generations.”, before the held material “Yahweh is faithful in all his words, and loving in all his deeds.” (web:Ps.145.13, whose verse_map_web entry records poetry_lines 3 against poetry_lines 1 for every other verse in this span). So MT carries two cola, not 'one sentence', and the variant is the third sentence of the WEB verse, not the second - a series ordinal that byte-settles the other way. Separately, 'nun-initial' is a letter property of a Hebrew line that is in neither staged witness's MT bytes: psalm_device_inventory.json licenses only 'nun is the letter Ps 145 lacks' (acrostics.145.letters_missing), and the skeleton sweep above returns 0 verses in Ps 145.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.145.14-16 re-derived. Hebrew byte-tier at cited refs: סוֹמֵ֣ךְ (oshb:Ps.145.14), עֵֽינֵי (oshb:Ps.145.15), פּוֹתֵ֥חַ (oshb:Ps.145.16). The samekh-ayin-pe run matches acrostics.145.first_letters_mt at the positions immediately after the missing nun, and the row's letter-skip observation at the seam is correct - psalm_device_inventory.json acrostics.145 records letters_missing = nun and mem is the preceding letter at oshb:Ps.145.13. The span is defensible on that tier-1 acrostic warrant. Its second cohesion signal, however, is byte-false: the three verses do not share one grammatical subject and there is an addressee shift inside the span.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[1] asserts that 'all 3 verses share the same grammatical subject (Yahweh) and predicate pattern (participle + object) without an addressee shift'; the bytes show a third-person-to-second-person addressee shift at web:Ps.145.14|web:Ps.145.15 and a different subject in web:Ps.145.15.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.145.14 predicates about Yahweh in the third person - סוֹמֵ֣ךְ יְ֭הוָה - matching “Yahweh upholds all who fall, and raises up all those who are bowed down.” (web:Ps.145.14). oshb:Ps.145.15 has a different subject and turns to direct address: עֵֽינֵי כֹ֭ל is the subject, and the verse carries the 2ms forms אֵלֶ֣יךָ and וְאַתָּ֤ה נֽוֹתֵן, matching “The eyes of all wait for you. You give them their food in due season.” (web:Ps.145.15). oshb:Ps.145.16 stays in second person - פּוֹתֵ֥חַ אֶת יָדֶ֑ךָ - matching “You open your hand, and satisfy the desire of every living thing.” (web:Ps.145.16). The addressee shift the signal denies is the strongest discourse seam inside this row's own span and it falls at the row's first internal boundary; the row's confidence of high rests partly on a warrant its own substrate contradicts.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.145.17-21 re-derived. Hebrew byte-tier at cited refs: צַדִּ֣יק (oshb:Ps.145.17), תְּהִלַּ֥ת יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.145.21). Tsade-qof-resh-shin-tav closes acrostics.145.first_letters_mt, and 5 letters here plus 3+4+6+3 in the other Ps 145 rows tiles the inventory's 21-letter string exactly. The tehillah inclusio is real: the title noun at oshb:Ps.145.1 and the construct at oshb:Ps.145.21 share the h-l-l root, and the row cites both ends. The span is sound. The rejected_alternative's discriminating warrant, however, is falsified by the row's own closing verse.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative rests on 'the catalog runs unbroken tsade through tav with no addressee or mode shift inside it', but web:Ps.145.21 shifts both voice and mode - back to the first-person speaker and into a volitive.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.145.17-20 are uniformly third-person predication about Yahweh (צַדִּ֣יק יְ֭הוָה, קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה, שׁוֹמֵ֣ר יְ֭הוָה). oshb:Ps.145.21 opens תְּהִלַּ֥ת יְהוָ֗ה יְֽדַבֶּ֫ר פִּ֥י, whose subject is the 1cs-suffixed פִּ֥י, and continues with the waw-prefixed volitive וִיבָרֵ֣ךְ taking כָּל בָּ֭שָׂר as its subject. WEB renders exactly that: “Yahweh preserves all those who love him, but he will destroy all the wicked.” (web:Ps.145.20) against “My mouth will speak the praise of Yahweh. Let all flesh bless his holy name forever and ever.” (web:Ps.145.21). The rejected split the row weighs (web:Ps.145.17-18 against web:Ps.145.19-21) is still correctly rejected, but the warrant used to reject it is byte-false, and any replacement warrant has to survive the test that kills this one.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.146.1-2 re-derived. Ps 146 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json psalms.146 rule=identity, 10/10, web_title false; verse_map_web has no Ps.146.0 entry), so no title pseudo-ref and no dual-cite arithmetic apply. The hallelu-Yah frame claim checks exactly: הַֽלְלוּ יָ֡הּ collates byte-tier at oshb:Ps.146.1 (skeleton-only collision at oshb:Ps.146.10, so the cited ref is the byte-grade one), and psalm_device_inventory.json halleluyah.verse_initial lists Ps.146.1 among 11 refs with counts.verse_initial = 11 - the row's digit and object are both right. The seam at web:Ps.146.2|web:Ps.146.3 is sound on content. But both of the row's discourse characterizations of web:Ps.146.1 are byte-false, and one of them is the discriminator the rejected_alternative leans on; the same false premise recurs on the other side of this seam, so the cure is one edit installed on both rows at the seam 146:2|146:3.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[1] claims 'the first-person cohortative register (I will praise, I will sing praises) runs unbroken across both verses', but web:Ps.146.1 contains no first-person form at all - it is two commands plus a vocative.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.146.1 reads הַֽלְלוּ יָ֡הּ הַלְלִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י אֶת יְהוָֽה: הַֽלְלוּ יָ֡הּ is the frame formula addressed to a plural audience and הַלְלִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י is a feminine-singular command with its vocative, matching “Praise Yah! Praise Yahweh, my soul.” (web:Ps.146.1) - no 1cs verb and no 1cs suffix on any verb in the verse. The cohortative register the signal describes begins only at oshb:Ps.146.2, אֲהַלְלָ֣ה and אֲזַמְּרָ֖ה, matching “While I live, I will praise Yahweh. I will sing praises to my God as long as I exist.” (web:Ps.146.2). The register therefore runs across one verse of the two, not unbroken across both.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative discriminates the seam by saying web:Ps.146.3's imperative arrives 'with no shared addressee', but the plural addressee of web:Ps.146.3 is the same plural addressee already commanded at web:Ps.146.1.
challenges.evidence: The frame formula at oshb:Ps.146.1 is הַֽלְלוּ - plural - and the admonition at oshb:Ps.146.3 opens אַל תִּבְטְח֥וּ, whose verb carries the same plural ending, matching “Don’t put your trust in princes, in a son of man in whom there is no help.” (web:Ps.146.3) against “Praise Yah!” (web:Ps.146.1). The addressee is shared, so 'no shared addressee' cannot carry the seam; the workable discriminator is the change of speech-act object (praise of Yah against warning about human helpers), not addressee identity. Labeling web:Ps.146.1-2 collectively as 'the cohortative vow' compounds the same misreading of web:Ps.146.1.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.146.3-4 re-derived. אַל תִּבְטְח֥וּ collates byte-tier at oshb:Ps.146.3. The span is sound: oshb:Ps.146.4 keeps the third-person subject introduced at oshb:Ps.146.3 (תֵּצֵ֣א ר֭וּחוֹ, יָשֻׁ֣ב), matching “His spirit departs, and he returns to the earth. In that very day, his thoughts perish.” (web:Ps.146.4), and the beatitude at oshb:Ps.146.5 opens a positively framed unit, so both seams hold. pmarks_Ps.json records a paseq seg at Ps.146.3 but the row makes no seg-layer claim, which is correct. The defect is the row's fresh-speech-act warrant, which is the mirror image of the false premise on the other side of the seam at 146:2|146:3 - one cure, both rows.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[0] asserts that the negative imperative at web:Ps.146.3 'has no imperative counterpart earlier in the psalm'; oshb:Ps.146.1 carries two, one of them in the same plural form.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.146.1 reads הַֽלְלוּ יָ֡הּ הַלְלִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י אֶת יְהוָֽה - הַֽלְלוּ is a plural command and הַלְלִ֥י is a singular command with the vocative נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י - rendered “Praise Yah! Praise Yahweh, my soul.” (web:Ps.146.1). The row's own verse opens אַל תִּבְטְח֥וּ, whose verb carries the same plural ending as הַֽלְלוּ, rendered “Don’t put your trust in princes, in a son of man in whom there is no help.” (web:Ps.146.3). The psalm's first command is therefore two verses earlier and shares the addressee number; what is fresh at web:Ps.146.3 is the object and the polarity, not the psalm's first imperative. The seam survives on that reworded warrant, but the signal as written is byte-false and the row's confidence of high is set on it.

reviews.reasoning: Span web:Ps.146.5-10 re-derived and it holds on every point I could test. All seven Hebrew runs collate at byte tier against their cited refs: אַשְׁרֵ֗י (oshb:Ps.146.5), עֹשֶׂ֤ה (oshb:Ps.146.6; identical pointing also at oshb:Ps.146.7, and the row cites 146.6 for the opening occurrence and names MT 146:7 separately in prose), הַשֹּׁמֵ֖ר אֱמֶ֣ת לְעוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ps.146.6), פֹּ֘קֵ֤חַ (oshb:Ps.146.8), שֹׁ֘מֵ֤ר (oshb:Ps.146.9; skeleton-only collision at oshb:Ps.146.6, so the cited ref is byte-grade), אֱלֹהַ֣יִךְ צִ֭יּוֹן (oshb:Ps.146.10), הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.146.10). I re-derived the participle count independently from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings and reach the row's 9 across MT 146:6-9: two at oshb:Ps.146.6 (עֹשֶׂ֤ה, הַשֹּׁמֵ֖ר), three at oshb:Ps.146.7 (עֹשֶׂ֤ה, נֹתֵ֣ן, מַתִּ֥יר), three at oshb:Ps.146.8 (פֹּ֘קֵ֤חַ, זֹקֵ֣ף, אֹהֵ֥ב), one at oshb:Ps.146.9 (שֹׁ֘מֵ֤ר), with the two finite forms the row names closing oshb:Ps.146.9 (יְעוֹדֵ֑ד, יְעַוֵּֽת) - WEB agrees throughout, “who executes justice for the oppressed; who gives food to the hungry. Yahweh frees the prisoners.” (web:Ps.146.7) and “Yahweh preserves the foreigners. He upholds the fatherless and widow, but he turns the way of the wicked upside down.” (web:Ps.146.9). The frame close checks against the inventory: halleluyah.verse_final lists Ps.146.10 with counts.verse_final = 13, matching the row's digit and object, and the row correctly pairs it with the verse-initial occurrence at oshb:Ps.146.1. The addressee shift at the close is disclosed rather than glossed over - אֱלֹהַ֣יִךְ carries a 2fs suffix and the row calls it a kingship declaration addressed to Zion, matching “Yahweh will reign forever; your God, O Zion, to all generations.” (web:Ps.146.10). Two observations, neither filed as a defect: 'byte-counted' labels a form claim the staged extract cannot machine-verify (verse_map_oshb.json carries text/language/web only - no morphology layer), so the accurate label is a byte-anchored re-derivation, which the row makes possible by naming all nine tokens; and pmarks_Ps.json records paseq segs at Ps.146.6-10 that the row does not cite, correctly, since it makes no seg-layer claim. Confidence medium is right for a six-verse row whose internal cohesion is a participle chain rather than a hard seam.
